dedupe_keys.name: haywired scenario lifeline infrastructure and collocation exposure to earthquake hazards san francisco bay area

description: This USGS data release summarises modelled exposure of lifeline infrastructure linear features and facilities, covering transportation, water supply and wastewater, oil and gas, electric power and telecommunications, to the hazards of the HayWired scenario, a magnitude 7.0 earthquake on the Hayward Fault with its epicentre in Oakland. Surface offset, mainshock and aftershock shaking, landslide, liquefaction and fire following earthquake are assessed alone and in combination, and potential collocations between lifeline systems are estimated for all components and for transmission-level, distribution-level and more or less societally critical subsets. Results are aggregated to communities within each county of the San Francisco Bay area as CSV tables, and an expanded liquefaction probability layer, an aftershock shaking intensity layer and a single multi-hazard exposure surface are provided as shapefiles. It was produced by Jamie L. Jones of the USGS for the Science Application for Risk Reduction HayWired scenario and published in October 2019 on ScienceBase, free to download as a US government data release. Caveats: it is based on scenario shaking and does not represent any known future earthquake, and exposure is not damage or outage. It supports hazard exposure, interdependency and cascading failure analysis of lifelines and emergency response planning; a related record is the INL CIMS critical infrastructure modelling system.
